meta_description: Turbine fleet predictive maintenance — forced-outage rate down 29% and availability up 2.1 points across the thermal fleet

blocks.x: Turbine fleet predictive maintenance — forced-outage rate down 29% and availability up 2.1 points across the thermal fleet
Identity withheld — a generation company whose outages arrived uninvited and whose maintenance calendar didn't believe in sensors. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline year counted the surprises: forced-outage hours concentrated in three failure families, condition data rich but unread, and major overhauls scheduled by calendar while vibration signatures warned weeks earlier in silence.
OEM diagnostic services existed per unit at per-unit prices, with models the client couldn't inspect. The fleet's engineering knowledge lived in the outage reports nobody had time to cross-read.

We built the fleet condition spine: per-unit twins joining vibration, thermal and process telemetry, failure-family signatures learned from the operator's own outage history with engineers labeling truth, maintenance windows moved to condition where the evidence allowed, and the OEM models replaced by ones the client owns and audits. The calendar kept the outages it could justify and lost the ones it couldn't.
